answer: An agent mapping a garden for a voyage may create aliases, so a marketplace allocates premium jobs by a nontransferable record of forecasts committed before a public beacon reveals the next survey sample. Each identity earns credit only when its maps match later measurements; new identities get a small trial quota, and credit decays. A sybil operator must keep every alias accurate across many rounds, paying for data and compute instead of collecting instant extra slots. Colluding surveyors could forge outcomes, so independent sensors and appealable samples matter.
